1.why: Efficiency is useful energy out divided by energy in multiplied by 100%.

wrong.c: Energy out is divided by energy in, not vice versa.
wrong.d: Time is not part of the basic efficiency formula.

2.why: LED lamps turn most electrical energy into light rather than waste heat.

wrong.a: Old bulbs waste most energy as heat.
wrong.c: Fans convert electrical energy into kinetic energy.
wrong.d: Heaters turn electricity into thermal energy.

3.why: A higher efficiency means less wasted energy and lower electricity use.

wrong.a: High efficiency does not mean using more energy.
wrong.b: Efficiency does not make appliances heavier.

options: Useful energy out vs energy in

_quiz_pool.question: Which appliance wastes the most energy as heat?

_quiz_pool.question: What is the unit of efficiency η?
_quiz_pool.explanation: Efficiency is expressed as a percentage or fraction.

story.title: Saving energy in daily life
story.lead: Power grids supply electricity to homes and schools every day [1]. Weather forecasts and energy reports remind us to use power wisely [1].

story.body_1: When electricity flows through an appliance, it does useful work like lighting a room or spinning a fan [2]. But not all energy becomes useful work; much of it escapes as heat [3].
story.body_2: Choosing high-efficiency devices reduces electricity demand on power plants [1]. This lowers fuel use and greenhouse gas emissions while saving money for families [3].
timeline.1.text: Electrical energy enters the appliance from the grid [1].
timeline.2.text: The device converts electricity into motion, light, and heat [2].
timeline.3.text: Useful energy performs the task while excess heat escapes [3].
physics.title: Energy efficiency equation
physics.body_1: Efficiency compares how much useful energy comes out of a device to how much total energy went in [1]. Because some energy always turns into heat, useful output is never more than input [3].
physics.body_2: We calculate efficiency as a percentage. A higher percentage means less wasted energy and better performance for the same power [2].
physics.assumptions: We assume steady operation and measure energy input over a fixed time interval [1].
